title: Buddy Bolden's band and personnel
summary: He lists the men in Bolden's band, how Dusen joined, and remembers hearing them at Funky Butt.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Where did you hear them play? Huh? Where did you hear the Bowling Band play?

What did I hear them play? I had a place on Padilla Street, on this side of the place, used to call it Funky Buddy. I came over and played with my brother. All you could hear once. During that time, the gloves were all around him. Got a place out here. Out by the base, the gloves. Where the auditorium is. By the auditorium. All right.

Buddy leaves Carnish go. What happened to Willie Carnish? He left him go. He fired him. He took four hours. He left him. He took four hours. He left him. He took Frank. Now, the job, Frank had all his job at all fellows on his. Then, says, Frank must tell him, he'd always advertise himself with allergies. Told him, dude's riding the car. Well, they're bowling with me. King Bowling. And they're the loudest horn in the world. They're the loudest horn in the world. The loudest horn in the world. Uh-huh. So, Frank came to all the fellows' horn with a new band there. He came there, but he still kept Frank Lewis, a granddad player. And they had Brock Lumpfurt, a guitar player. And they had Dee Dee with him. Bowling's band, in other words. Bowling. He had Franklin Bowling's band. That's why he combined with Bowling. Bowling was, ooh, taller man than Mr. Bill. Heavisette. He was a young man.
Dark? No, he was, he was brown-skinned. He wasn't black. He was a brown-skinned fellow.
Well, then you heard him when he came back, when the band came back? Oh, yeah, sure.

Because my brother had brought him out by the funky butt. My brother's a dancer. But my brother and Frankie Deuston, they come up together. They're raised up together now, geez. Frankie Deuston, Jimmy Palau, my brother, Victor Mineta, they're all raised. My brother was a dancer, though. They warned him he had a very good talent for music. He could play a nice cornet. But he didn't like that. He was a fellow who liked his hard work. He worked in SPR, 38 years.
